mainTopic: Whose view the משנה follows, רבי יוחנן's rules on the lineage of non-Jews and converts, and the source that קידושין do not take hold with עריות
overview: The גמרא finishes testing whether the משנה follows רבי יהודה or רבי יוסי. It concludes that a repeated phrase like 'כל מקום' can be there just to keep the wording consistent, so the משנה can fit רבי יוסי. Then it explains רבי יוחנן's rule, reported by רבין. Among non-Jews, the child follows the father, as a ברייתא about buying slaves shows. Once the parents convert, the child follows the more flawed parent, as in an עמוני man married to an מצרית woman. Next, the גמרא looks for the source that קידושין do not take hold with close relatives, starting from 'והיתה לאיש אחר'. After several back-and-forths, that פסוק is used up on אחות אשה. A comparison to her fails for אשת אח and אשת איש, so a הקש from ויקרא 18:29 ties all the עריות to אחות אשה. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new challenge to that הקש.

steps.title: Under רבי יהודה, the second 'any case' includes a convert who married a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes showing that if the משנה follows רבי יהודה, the second 'כל מקום' has a clear job: to include a גר who married a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase 'any case' in the latter clause comes to include a convert who married a ממזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its 'this works nicely under רבי יהודה' list. This sets up the challenge against רבי יוסי that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a גר may not marry a ממזרת. So that marriage counts as 'betrothal with a transgression,' and the latter clause's 'any case' (the child follows the flawed parent) is there to include it. Under רבי יהודה, every phrase in the משנה has a job.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
To include, to bring in an extra case
A convert
A woman born from a forbidden union (a female ממזר)

phrases.english: 'Any case' of the latter clause
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's line about betrothal that involves a transgression, where the child follows the flawed parent.

phrases.english: comes to include a convert who married a mamzeret.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כׇּל מָקוֹם״ דְּסֵיפָא – לְאֵתוֹיֵי גֵּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא מַמְזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the 'granted, under רבי יהודה' list, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יהודה, the latter 'כל מקום' includes a גר married to a ממזרת.

steps.title: Under רבי יוסי, the second 'any case' seems to add nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי יוסי, the first 'כל מקום' and the 'איזו זו' are explained, but the second 'כל מקום' has nothing to add.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the משנה follows רבי יוסי: the 'any case' of the first clause is as we said, and 'which is this' is as we said. But what does the 'any case' of the latter clause come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the משנה follows רבי יוסי, because one of its phrases would then be useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows a גר to marry a ממזרת, so that case is not a 'transgression' marriage. That leaves the latter 'כל מקום' with no extra case to include. A משנה should not have a wasted phrase, so this looks like a problem for רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה
As we said earlier
What does it come to include?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: But if you say it is Rabbi Yosei,
'any case' of the first clause is as we said,
'which is this' is as we said,
but 'any case' of the latter clause
comes to include what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets רבי יוסי against the smooth reading under רבי יהודה from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוסי, the latter 'כל מקום' has no case to include, so it would be a wasted phrase.

steps.title: Counter-question: רבי יהודה has a repeated phrase too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a counter-question: even under רבי יהודה, the second 'איזו זו' seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, for רבי יהודה, why do I need 'which is this' of the latter clause?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around and shows that רבי יהודה faces the same problem. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every phrase must add something, then רבי יהודה also has a phrase, the second 'איזו זו', that adds nothing new. So the argument 'a phrase would be useless' proves too much, because it would knock out רבי יהודה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning (a counter-challenge)
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, for Rabbi Yehuda,
why do I need 'which is this' of the latter clause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יוסי by showing that the challenge in step 2 also hits רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption behind step 2 that every phrase must add a new case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יהודה, the second 'איזו זו' would also be extra, so the assumption cannot be right.

steps.title: Repeated wording for consistency
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats phrases in the latter clause just to match the first clause. That explains 'איזו זו' under רבי יהודה and 'כל מקום' under רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: since it taught 'which is this' in the first clause, it taught 'which is this' in the latter clause. So too, since it taught 'any case' in the first clause, it also taught 'any case' in the latter clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: sometimes the משנה repeats a phrase only so that both halves are worded the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה must accept that the second 'איזו זו' is there just for matching style, רבי יוסי can say the same about the second 'כל מקום'. So the משנה can follow רבי יוסי after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (here: it repeated the wording to match)
That it taught
So too, the same here

steps.whatToRemember: A phrase in a משנה is not always there to add a new case. Sometimes it is only repeated so the two clauses match (אַיְּידֵי).

phrases.english: Rather: since it taught 'which is this' in the first clause,
it taught 'which is this' in the latter clause.
So too,
since it taught 'any case' in the first clause,
it also taught 'any case' in the latter clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the counter-question in step 3 and so answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every phrase in the משנה must add a new case, so רבי יוסי does not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeated phrases can be there only for matching style, so the משנה can fit רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: among the nations follow the father; after conversion follow the flawed parent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבין's report that רבי יוחנן said: among non-Jews the child follows the father, and if the parents converted the child follows the more flawed parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן says: Among the nations, follow the male. If they converted, follow the flawed one of the two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement it mentioned earlier in this discussion and now quotes it in full so it can study it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules. For non-Jews from different nations, the child's status follows the father. Once the parents have become גרים, the child gets the status of whichever parent's lineage is lower.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself, returning to a statement quoted earlier
When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Follow the male (the father)
The flawed one, the parent with the lower lineage
They converted

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
Among the nations, follow the male.
If they converted, follow the flawed one of the two.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to a statement quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Among non-Jews the child follows the father. After the parents convert, the child follows the more flawed parent.

steps.title: What does 'among the nations follow the male' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule means in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'among the nations, follow the male'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the first rule. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a real case where following the non-Jewish father makes a difference to the child's status.

keyTerms.meaning: Among the nations (non-Jews)

phrases.english: What is 'among the nations, follow the male'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first half of the rule in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case that shows what 'follow the male' among the nations means.

steps.title: The ברייתא about buying the son of a non-Jew and a Canaanite woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that asks for a source: a non-Jew who fathers a son with a Canaanite woman, and that son may be bought as a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that if one of the nations had relations with a Canaanite woman and fathered a son, you are permitted to buy him as a slave?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to explain the rule. The ברייתא opens with a 'from where do we know' question, and the next step gives its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case shows 'follow the male' at work. The son follows his non-Canaanite father, so he does not count as a Canaanite, and that is why he may be bought as a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
From where do we know? (asking for a source)
A Canaanite woman
To buy him as a slave

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. This is only its question; its source and answer come in steps 8 and 9.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
From where do we know regarding one of the nations
who had relations with a Canaanite woman and fathered a son,
that you are permitted to buy him as a slave?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question in step 6 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is a non-Jew's son by a Canaanite woman. He follows his father, so he may be bought as a slave. The source is given in step 8.

steps.title: The verse that allows buying children of foreign residents
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings its source: a פסוק that allows buying slaves from the children of foreigners living among us.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And also from the children of the residents who live among you, from them you may buy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 7 now gives its source. A פסוק says we may buy slaves from the children of foreigners living among us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the case was a non-Jew from the other nations who had a son with a כנענית woman. This פסוק shows that such a son may be bought as a slave. That only works if the son follows his non-Canaanite father.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a source)
Residents, foreigners living in the land
You may buy

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And also of the children of the residents
who sojourn with you, of them you may buy."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְגַם מִבְּנֵי הַתּוֹשָׁבִים הַגָּרִים עִמָּכֶם מֵהֶם תִּקְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that supports the case the ברייתא raised in step 7
steps.raayaObject: A son of a non-Canaanite father and a כנענית mother may be bought as a slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 25:45, 'וגם מבני התושבים הגרים עמכם מהם תקנו'

steps.title: A son of a Canaanite father may not be bought
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that even a son of a Canaanite father and a mother from the other nations could be bought, then rejects this from the words 'which they fathered in your land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even if a Canaanite slave had relations with a maidservant from the other nations and fathered a son, you could buy that son as a slave. So the verse says: 'which they fathered in your land.' You may buy from those who were born in your land, but not from those who live in your land as natives.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא flips the case: now the father is Canaanite and the mother is from another nation. The פסוק teaches that this son may not be bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Born in your land' describes children of foreign fathers, and these may be bought. 'Living in your land' describes the Canaanite nations themselves, and these may not be bought. Since the son of a Canaanite father counts as Canaanite, this proves the child follows the father, which is the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces a possibility that will be rejected)
Maidservant
Permitted
Those born

steps.whatToRemember: Among non-Jews, the child follows the father. A son of a Canaanite father is Canaanite, even if his mother is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule from step 5.

phrases.english: One might have thought that even a slave
phrases.notes: Here 'slave' means a man from the seven Canaanite nations.

phrases.english: who had relations with a maidservant from the other nations
and fathered a son,
that you are permitted to buy him as a slave?
The verse states: "Which they have fathered in your land"
from those born in your land,
and not from those who live in your land.
phrases.notes: 'Those who live in your land' are the Canaanite nations themselves. A child with a Canaanite father counts as one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף עֶבֶד שֶׁבָּא עַל שִׁפְחָה מִן הָאוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by limiting the פסוק of step 8 to children of non-Canaanite fathers
steps.raayaObject: Among non-Jews the child follows the father
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'אשר הולידו בארצכם' in ויקרא 25:45

steps.title: Which case does 'follow the more flawed parent' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the second half of רבי יוחנן's rule is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If they converted, follow the more flawed of the two.' What case is this talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second half of רבי יוחנן's rule and asks for a real case. This sets up a two-part search for the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once parents convert, their lineage matters for whom their child may marry. The גמרא wants a case where one parent truly has a worse status than the other.

keyTerms.meaning: They converted
Flawed, of blemished lineage
In what case?

phrases.english: "If they converted, follow
the flawed one of the two"
In which case?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְגַּיְּירוּ הַלֵּךְ אַחַר הַפָּגוּם שֶׁבִּשְׁנֵיהֶם בְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule and turns to the second half
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where converted parents have different levels of flawed lineage

steps.title: Not an Egyptian man with an Ammonite woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the case is an מצרי man married to an עמונית woman, because an עמונית has no flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is an Egyptian man who married an Ammonite woman, what flaw is there? The Torah says 'an Ammonite man,' not an Ammonite woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one case and throws it out right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on marrying into the community applies only to עמוני men, not עמונית women. So in this case the mother has no flaw, and there is no 'more flawed' parent to compare. The rule must be talking about the opposite case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a suggestion that will be rejected)
An Egyptian convert
An Ammonite man is banned, not an Ammonite woman

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume an עמונית convert is banned like an עמוני. Only the men are banned, and the women may marry into the community.

phrases.english: If you say it is an Egyptian man who married an Ammonite woman,
what flaw is there?
"An Ammonite" — and not an Ammonite woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects a first possible answer to step 10's question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the case of an מצרי man with an עמונית woman
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An עמונית has no flaw, so neither parent is 'more flawed'

steps.title: An Ammonite man who married an Egyptian woman
steps.stepSummary: The case is an עמוני man married to an מצרית woman. A son follows the father and a daughter follows the mother, so the child always ends up with the flawed status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is an Ammonite man who married an Egyptian woman. If the child is a boy, put him after his father. If the child is a girl, put her after her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case and shows how 'follow the more flawed one' works in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy follows his עמוני father, and an עמוני man is banned forever. A girl cannot get a flaw from her father, because עמונית women are permitted, so she follows her מצרית mother. That makes her a second-generation מצרית, who is still banned. Either way, the child takes the more flawed status.

keyTerms.meaning: Cast him after him (he follows that parent's status)
Male
Female
An Egyptian woman convert

steps.whatToRemember: 'Follow the more flawed parent' means the child gets whichever status is worse for that child. A son of an עמוני is banned as an עמוני, and a daughter is banned as a second-generation מצרית.

phrases.english: Rather, it is an Ammonite man who married an Egyptian woman,
and if the child is a male,
cast him after his own [father],
and if the child is a female,
cast her after her own [mother].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the case in step 11, gives the correct case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עמוני man with an מצרית woman: a son follows the father (banned forever) and a daughter follows the mother (second-generation מצרית)

steps.title: Source for the משנה's 'whoever cannot have קידושין with him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about a woman who cannot have קידושין with this man and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Any woman who cannot have קידושין with him.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: it quotes the next line of the משנה and asks where it comes from. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that when a woman cannot have קידושין with this man, but can with others, the child is a ממזר. The גמרא wants a source that קידושין with such a woman, a close relative, does not take effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
From where are these words learned?

phrases.english: Any woman who cannot have betrothal with him.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עָלָיו קִידּוּשִׁין מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי יוחנן's rule to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that קידושין with a forbidden relative does not take effect

steps.title: 'To another man' means to others, not to relatives
steps.stepSummary: Several chains of teachers report that the פסוק 'and she becomes another man's' teaches that קידושין works with others but not with close relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן (and some trace it to רבי ינאי), and רב אחא son of רבא traced it to רבי יוסי הגלילי: The verse says, 'And she leaves his house, and goes, and becomes another man's.' This means to others, not to relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about a divorced woman remarrying. The word 'another' is read to mean 'others, not relatives.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said she marries a man. Saying 'another man' teaches that she can marry other people, but not her close relatives. So קידושין with a forbidden relative does not take effect at all, which is the משנה's category of 'אין לה עליו קידושין.'

keyTerms.meaning: And they traced it back (to an earlier teacher)
To others and not to relatives

steps.whatToRemember: קידושין with a close relative (an ערוה) does not take effect, learned from 'והיתה לאיש אחר': to others, not to relatives.
steps.whyThisMatters: This source is the basis for the משנה's rule that the child of a union where קידושין cannot take effect is a ממזר.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said,
and they traced it to the name of Rabbi Yannai;
and Rav Acha son of Rava

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי:
phrases.english: traced it to the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
The verse says:
"And she leaves his house and goes
and becomes another man's"
to others, and not to relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's request for a source
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'והיתה לאיש אחר' (דברים 24:2) teach that קידושין takes effect with others but not with close relatives

steps.title: Maybe 'another' only excludes the son
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges the דרשה: maybe the word 'אחר' only means 'but not the husband's son.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objects: But maybe 'to another man' means only 'and not to the son'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks the proof from Step 14. He says the word 'another' could be teaching something much narrower than 'no relatives.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 read 'אחר' broadly: others yes, relatives no. רבי אבא offers a narrower reading: it only blocks her from marrying her husband's son. If that is right, we lose our source for all the other relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects, challenges (a strong attack on a statement)
But say / maybe it means
Another (man), from the פסוק 'והיתה לאיש אחר'

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba objects to this:
But say: "to another" and not to a son!
phrases.notes: He means the husband's son. So the woman could not marry her own stepson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The broad reading of 'אחר' as excluding all relatives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could be read narrowly, as excluding only the son.

steps.title: The son already has his own verse
steps.stepSummary: The son's case is written openly in another פסוק, so 'אחר' must be teaching about all relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a son it is written openly: 'A man shall not take his father's wife.' So why do I need 'another'? Learn from it: others yes, relatives no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אבא. The Torah already speaks about the son clearly somewhere else, so the word 'another' is not needed for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. The son is already covered by 'לא יקח איש את אשת אביו', so 'אחר' would add nothing if it only meant the son. It must therefore teach the wider rule: no קידושין with any relative.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, written explicitly
Why do I need it? (the word seems extra)
Learn from this
Close relatives

steps.title: Maybe both verses are about the son
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps both פסוקים speak about the son: one forbids it from the start, the other makes it fail after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that both this verse and that verse are about the son: this one is about doing it from the start, and that one is about after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Maybe 'אחר' is not extra at all, because each פסוק about the son does a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא יקח' could just mean 'don't do it.' 'אחר' could add that if he did it anyway, the קידושין do not work. Then both words are needed for the son, and there is still no source for other relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that
From the start, before acting
After the fact, once it was already done

this one is about from the start,

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both פסוקים could be needed for the son, each for a different stage.

steps.title: The son is already covered by a קל וחומר from a wife's sister
steps.stepSummary: We don't need a פסוק for the son, because a קל וחומר from אחות אשה already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'from the start' rule is learned from a wife's sister: if a wife's sister, which only carries כרת, cannot receive קידושין, then relatives punished by בית דין with death, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the son's case does not need its own פסוק at all. It can be learned through a קל וחומר from the case of a wife's sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a wife's sister, which carries only כרת, קידושין do not take hold. A father's wife carries the even stricter punishment of death by בית דין, so surely קידושין do not work there either. Since the son is already covered this way, 'אחר' is free to teach the general rule about relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife's sister (forbidden while the wife is alive)
Spiritual cutting-off, a punishment from Heaven
קידושין take hold / work
Death penalties carried out by the court
All the more so (קל וחומר)

phrases.english: The 'from the start' rule comes from a wife's sister:
Just as a wife's sister, which is punished with כרת,
קידושין do not take hold with her,

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then those liable to court-imposed death, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים are needed for the son
steps.terutzMaskana: The son is covered by a קל וחומר from אחות אשה, so 'אחר' stays extra
steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר goes from the lighter case to the stricter one. אחות אשה carries only כרת, while a father's wife carries death by בית דין, which is stricter.

steps.title: Maybe both verses are about a wife's sister
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the 'don't take' פסוק and 'אחר' both speak about אחות אשה: one from the start, one after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that both this verse and that verse are about a wife's sister: this one from the start, and that one after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the same pattern again, this time with אחות אשה. Maybe the two פסוקים split the work for her case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about a wife's sister could just forbid the marriage. 'אחר' would then teach that if it happened anyway, the קידושין fail. On this reading, 'אחר' would be about אחות אשה and not a general rule for all relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: This one (pointing to one of the two פסוקים)
About (the case of) a wife's sister

phrases.english: But say: both this and that are about a wife's sister,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the פסוק about a wife's sister, ויקרא 18:18; 'that' is 'another man's', דברים 24:2.

phrases.english: this one from the start, that one after the fact!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies Step 17's pattern to אחות אשה
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for 'אחר' as a general rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both פסוקים could be split between 'from the start' and 'after the fact' for אחות אשה.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that both פסוקים are about a wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the last suggestion. Both פסוקים are about אחות אשה, one for 'from the start' and one for 'after the fact.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not reject this reading; it accepts it. That means 'אחר' is now used up on אחות אשה, so the rule is proven only for her. The next step asks how the other עריות are learned, and steps 22–25 work out the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (an admission)

steps.whatToRemember: The final reading: 'לא תקח' and 'לאיש אחר' both speak about אחות אשה, one for 'from the start' and one for 'after the fact.' So far the rule that קידושין fail is proven only for her. The next steps look for a source for all the other עריות.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the suggestion of Step 19
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both פסוקים refer to אחות אשה: one forbids from the start, one makes the קידושין fail after the fact.

steps.title: What about all the other forbidden relations?
steps.stepSummary: We have a source for אחות אשה. Where do we learn that קידושין fail with the other עריות?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for a wife's sister. Where do we learn it for the other forbidden relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up what it proved so far, which is only about אחות אשה. Now it asks for a source for all the other עריות, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16–20 ended with both פסוקים being about אחות אשה. So the rule that קידושין do not take hold is proven only for her. The rest of the עריות still need a source.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for this)
The other forbidden relations
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found a source for a wife's sister;
the other forbidden relations, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה, שְׁאָר עֲרָיוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 20 and widens the question from אחות אשה to all עריות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that קידושין fail with all the עריות, not only with אחות אשה.

steps.title: Learning the other forbidden relations from a wife's sister
steps.stepSummary: Any ערוה punished by כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake is like אחות אשה, so קידושין do not take hold with her either.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from a wife's sister. A wife's sister is a forbidden relation, punished with כרת when done on purpose and a sin-offering when done by mistake, and קידושין do not take hold with her. So too any woman who is a forbidden relation with the same punishments: קידושין do not take hold with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing every other ערוה to אחות אשה. They share the same features, so they share the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a comparison built on shared features: being an ערוה, כרת for doing it on purpose, and חטאת for doing it by mistake. If another ערוה has all these features, it should also share the result that קידושין do not take hold. The weak point of this kind of comparison is that someone can point to a feature that makes the source case different, and that is what comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn it (from another case)
Singled out, written in the תורה
Doing it on purpose
Doing it by mistake
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment
קידושין do not take hold with her

phrases.english: We learn it from a wife's sister:
just as a wife's sister, who is specified,
phrases.notes: Specified means the תורה wrote her case openly, as the earlier steps showed.

phrases.english: is a forbidden relation
and one is liable to כרת for doing it on purpose
and to a sin-offering for doing it by mistake,
and betrothal does not take hold with her,
so too, any woman who is a forbidden relation
and one is liable to כרת for doing it on purpose
and to a sin-offering for doing it by mistake,
betrothal does not take hold with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלְפִינַן מֵאֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה: מָה אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All עריות that carry כרת and חטאת are compared to אחות אשה, so קידושין do not take hold with them.

steps.title: A brother's wife breaks the comparison
steps.stepSummary: Most עריות can be learned this way, but not אשת אח, because she becomes permitted for the מצוה of יבום and אחות אשה never does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, all the others can be learned this way. But a married woman and a brother's wife can be challenged: a wife's sister is never permitted even for a מצוה. Can you say the same about a brother's wife, who is permitted for a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the comparison works for most עריות but fails for two: אשת איש and אשת אח. Here it explains why אשת אח fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחות אשה is stricter: no מצוה ever permits her. אשת אח is forbidden, but she becomes permitted for יבום. A weaker איסור might let קידושין take hold, so we cannot learn אשת אח from the stricter אחות אשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part works
There is room to challenge (the comparison)
Permitted where there is a מצוה (here, יבום)
A brother's wife

steps.confusionAlert: This line names both אשת איש and אשת אח, but it only explains the problem with אשת אח. The problem with אשת איש comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Granted, all of them can be learned this way,
but a married woman and a brother's wife:
there is room to challenge it:
what about a wife's sister?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לָהּ הֶיתֵּר בִּמְקוֹם מִצְוָה –
phrases.english: She is never permitted, even where there is a מצוה.
Will you say the same about a brother's wife,
who is permitted where there is a מצוה?
phrases.notes: The מצוה here is יבום: when a man dies with no children, his brother marries the widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כּוּלְּהוּ אָתְיָין, אֶלָּא אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ וְאֵשֶׁת אָח – אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning אשת אח from אחות אשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אחות אשה is stricter because no מצוה ever permits her, while אשת אח is permitted for יבום. A rule from the stricter case cannot be carried over to the weaker one.

steps.title: A married woman breaks the comparison too
steps.stepSummary: אשת איש can become permitted through divorce while her husband is still alive. אחות אשה and אשת אח cannot be permitted while the person who causes the איסור is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: A married woman can also be challenged: these others are never permitted while the person who makes them forbidden is alive. Can you say the same about a married woman, who can become permitted while the one who makes her forbidden is still alive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the problem with אשת איש, the second case it named in step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's sister is forbidden only while the wife is alive. A brother's wife can become permitted only after the brother has died, through יבום when he left no children. Neither can be permitted while the person who causes the איסור is alive. A married woman can be, through a גט while her husband is alive. That makes her איסור weaker, so the comparison fails for her too.

keyTerms.meaning: These (the earlier cases)
During the life of the one who makes them forbidden
A married woman

phrases.english: A married woman can also be challenged:
what about these?
phrases.notes: These means אחות אשה and אשת אח, the cases we might try to learn from.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵין לָהּ הֶיתֵּר בְּחַיֵּי אוֹסְרָן –
phrases.english: They are not permitted while the one who makes them forbidden is alive.
Will you say the same about a married woman,
who can be permitted while the one who makes her forbidden is alive!
phrases.notes: Through a גט, her husband frees her while he is still alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the attack opened in step 23 by explaining the problem with אשת איש.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning אשת איש from אחות אשה (and אשת אח)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those cases are never permitted while the person causing the איסור is alive. אשת איש can be permitted by divorce during her husband's life, so her איסור is weaker and cannot be learned from them.

steps.title: A פסוק groups all forbidden relations together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונה (or רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע) brings ויקרא 18:29, which puts all the עריות together. So they all share the rule of אחות אשה: קידושין do not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יונה said, and some say it was רב הונא son of רב יהושע: the פסוק says, "Whoever does any of these abominations shall be cut off." All the forbidden relations are compared to a wife's sister. Just as קידושין do not take hold with a wife's sister, so too קידושין do not take hold with any of the forbidden relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The comparison by shared features has failed, so the גמרא brings a new source: a פסוק that joins all the עריות together into one group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison by shared features can be knocked down if one case has a weaker feature. A הקש works differently. The פסוק itself puts all the עריות in one group, so they share the rule even where their details differ. This covers אשת אח and אשת איש as well.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared through a הקש (a פסוק grouping them together)
Abominations

steps.whatToRemember: Comparing by shared features failed because of אשת אח (permitted for יבום) and אשת איש (permitted by divorce while her husband is alive). The final source is a הקש from ויקרא 18:29, which ties all the עריות to אחות אשה, so קידושין do not take hold with any of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule that קידושין never take hold with any of the עריות punished by כרת, including אשת איש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yona said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua:
The verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה מִכֹּל הַתּוֹעֵבֹת הָאֵלֶּה וְנִכְרְתוּ״,
phrases.english: "Whoever does any of these abominations shall be cut off,"

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת כּוּלָּם לַאֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: all the forbidden relations are compared to a wife's sister:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה לֹא תָּפְסִי בָּהּ קִידּוּשִׁין –
phrases.english: just as betrothal does not take hold with a wife's sister,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת כּוּלָּם לֹא תָּפְסִי בָּהּ קִידּוּשִׁין.
phrases.english: so too, betrothal does not take hold with any of the forbidden relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the failed comparison of steps 22–24 and gives a new source for step 21's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source: a הקש from a פסוק instead of a comparison by shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have learned the עריות from אחות אשה by shared features, but that fails for אשת אח and אשת איש.
steps.terutzMaskana: ויקרא 18:29 groups all the עריות with אחות אשה, so קידושין do not take hold with any of them.

steps.title: If so: the opening of a new challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the answer from ויקרא 18:29 for now and opens a challenge with the words 'If so'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so (if this rule really comes from that פסוק)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It says 'If so', which means: 'Suppose we learn this from the פסוק that groups all the עריות together. Then something else becomes hard to explain.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is said yet. The phrase only tells you that a challenge is coming, and that it is based on the answer we just heard in step 25. Keep that answer in mind, because the next words will push against it.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so": a stock opening that takes the last answer as true and then shows a problem it causes.
"If"
"So" or "like this": it points back to what was just said.

steps.confusionAlert: 'אי הכי' does not reject the previous answer by itself. It accepts that answer for the sake of argument and then shows a problem that follows from it.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: 'So' points back to step 25: learning that קידושין fail with all the עריות from ויקרא 18:29.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It takes the answer from step 25 as true and starts a challenge that grows out of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 25: all the עריות are learned together from ויקרא 18:29.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is only the opening formula. It accepts the step 25 answer for the sake of argument, and the problem that answer causes appears in the words that follow.
